theme: Sierra Gorda has begun a US$725 million brownfield copper expansion
why_surfaced: A ceremonial construction start on 2 October adds physical execution to a previously approved project, while owner disclosures quantify capex, capacity and output effects.

world_change: A producing Chilean copper-molybdenum mine has begun a major brownfield processing expansion.
pressure: Electrification and grid buildout increase long-run copper demand while new mine supply remains slow and capital intensive.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Ore-processing capacity, project delivery, water and power availability.
formation: KGHM and South32 approved and started a fourth grinding line expected to lift processing capacity about 25-26% and copper-equivalent production about 30% from FY31.
consequences: Higher mine throughput from existing infrastructure
Potential demand for mining equipment and contractors
evidence: South32 final investment approval and FY26 results

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 5 October scan; it was absent from the 3 October reading layer.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: Final investment approval, owner funding, quantified capacity gains and a physical construction start establish a coherent mechanism, while delivery is not yet complete.
strengthening_evidence: KGHM announced the construction launch on 2 October.
South32 confirms execution approval, capex timing and expected output effects.
break_conditions: Water, power or permitting constrains the new line
new_links: The July investment decision is now linked to an October construction start.

valuation_research: The project is disclosed at roughly US$21,000 per tonne of incremental copper-equivalent capacity using FY25 realised prices. A current security-level valuation and entry range were not established in this scan; future work should separate Sierra Gorda value from each owner's broader commodity portfolio and capital-allocation changes.

evidence.fact: KGHM says construction of the fourth grinding line has started and values the project at about US$725 million.
South32 says the joint venture approved execution, expects about US$725 million of capex over FY27-FY30 and about 30% higher copper-equivalent production from FY31.
Chile's mining ministry records the cornerstone ceremony, a 26% capacity increase and works beginning in early 2027.
evidence.english_summary: The ministry describes the fourth-line ceremony, US$725 million investment, expected 26% capacity increase, employment and mine-life context.

contradictions: The ceremonial start precedes the main works scheduled for early 2027.
Expected output is forecast rather than realised, and returns remain exposed to copper and molybdenum prices.
